key_insight: This paper studies how generalization improves when you scale both the number of trainable parameters and the amount of data in a feature-learning model, rather than treating one of them in isolation. It provides scaling-law insights for quadratic neural networks, helping explain the joint role of width and dataset size.
problem_solved: Most existing scaling-law theories focus on either data or compute in fixed-feature or infinite-width settings. This work addresses the missing question of how test error scales jointly with model width and sample size in a trainable, feature-learning neural network.
method: Analyze \(\ell_2\)-regularized empirical test error in a quadratic neural network setting.
Study how generalization changes as both the number of parameters and the number of training samples vary.
Derive scaling-law behavior in a regime that captures feature learning rather than only fixed-feature or infinite-width limits.
impact: For practitioners, this helps predict when adding parameters versus adding data will most improve performance. It can guide more efficient model scaling and dataset planning in settings where feature learning matters.

paper_title: How Width and Data Shape Generalization Scaling Laws in Quadratic Neural Networks
paper_authors: Julius Girardin, Emanuele Troiani, Yizhou Xu, Vittorio Erba, Florent Krzakala
